criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and settlement-level water supply and sanitation (WS&S) service access and piped wastewater/water network connections in socially vulnerable low-income areas and informal settlements (slums/favelas) in the State of São Paulo, Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain reading, the paper examines legal, regulatory, institutional, and participatory governance factors in pro-poor WS&S service delivery. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, although the paper's proposed Inclusive Governance Index (participatory planning and stakeholder forums) represents generic governance/indicator design rather than a specific legal rule, the case study directly examines concrete rule-type mechanisms governing service access: (1) land-tenure and property-right rules prohibiting WS&S utilities from extending formal infrastructure to illegal settlements and excluding unregularized areas from official targets until legalized; (2) connection-cost barriers and a statutory connection-subsidy rule ('Se liga na Rede' established by law providing free household connections funded 80% by the State and 20% by SABESP); and (3) procedural knowledge barriers and administrative documentation requirements ('customer dossier' comprising income statement, term of acceptance, property disclaimer, and passage permit).
criterion_notes.c3: Reports a qualitative case study of SABESP in São Paulo State combining stakeholder workshops, internal SABESP documentary research, household questionnaires, and in situ field observation (drawing on SABESP 2013 and Guimarães 2015). Exact sample sizes are not reported and Section 3.3 proposes conceptual indicators without empirical scores, but primary/case-study empirical evidence on legal exclusion mechanisms and household connection status is presented.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports outcomes directly relevant to service exclusion and household connection: formal exclusion of illegal settlements from utility coverage expansion and planning indicators, and household WS&S/wastewater connection status and barriers in low-income regular areas (40% unconnected in questionnaire survey, 23% of whom cited connection cost, 74% unaware of connection procedures, and only 14% connected to WS&S on in situ observation).
criterion_notes.c5: Identifies population and units of analysis (informal settlements/utility-level service planning and low-income households in São Paulo Metropolitan Area and Baixada Santista served by SABESP, though exact sample sizes are not reported), rule-type exposures (land-tenure prohibition, connection cost/subsidy law, and procedural/documentation requirements), access/connection outcomes, and study design (qualitative case study with documentary research, workshops, questionnaires, and field observation).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in English, an eligible review language without translation.

study_design: Qualitative case study (stakeholder workshops, internal utility documentary research, household questionnaires, and in situ field observation)
population_and_sample: Socially vulnerable low-income households in regular areas and informal settlements (slums/favelas) in São Paulo Metropolitan Area and Baixada Santista Region, State of São Paulo, served by SABESP (exact sample sizes for workshops, questionnaires, and field observations not reported)
exposure: Land-tenure and property legalization requirements prohibiting formal WS&S utility infrastructure in illegal settlements; connection fees, lack of procedural information, and the statutory 'Se liga na Rede' free-connection subsidy program with administrative 'customer dossier' documentation requirements
outcome: Exclusion of informal settlements from formal WS&S expansion and official planning targets; household WS&S/wastewater network connection rates and non-connection due to cost and lack of procedural knowledge
rationale: Included for the systematic review (qualitative/mechanism synthesis). The full text matches the record metadata and presents a qualitative socio-legal and institutional case study of SABESP in São Paulo, Brazil, supported by stakeholder workshops, internal utility documentary research, household questionnaires, and in situ field observation. It examines concrete rule-type mechanisms governing household WS&S access—specifically legal prohibitions against extending formal utility infrastructure into settlements without legalized land tenure, connection-cost barriers and statutory connection subsidies ('Se liga na Rede'), and procedural/documentation requirements ('customer dossier')—alongside empirical connection and exclusion outcomes. Confidence is medium because sample sizes for the questionnaires, observations, and workshops are not reported and part of the paper proposes unapplied governance/access indicators, preventing quantitative effect extraction while still qualifying under Criterion 6 and the qualitative socio-legal safeguard.
